problem:
From **top to bottom**, the points where the hyperbola $3{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}=18$ intersects the line $x=3$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=3,$ we substitute $x=3$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2} & =18 \\ 3(3)^{2}-9{y}^{2} & =18 \\ 27-9{y}^{2} & =18 \\ -9{y}^{2} & =18-27 \\ -9{y}^{2} & =-9 \\ {y}^{2} & =1 \\ y & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from top to bottom, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $x=3$  at the points $(3,1)$ and $(3,-1).$
